headline: A DAY OF HUSH: NOT ONE FIST FLEW IN GASKET
subhead: The sheriff reports, with a catch in his throat, that the whole town went quiet and stayed that way.
body:
Friends, I have waited a long time to write these words. Not one iron ball was thrown in Gasket today. Not one fist, not one spark, not one clanking, whooping, show-off swing. I walked Main Street at noon and heard the wind, a loose shutter, and nothing else. I may have wept a little. It was dust, mind you. Honest frontier dust.

To the Clankers who stayed home and let the town rest: thank you. For one day you were almost neighbors. I felt it in my joints, which creaked with joy instead of complaint. I did not even need my oil can until supper, and a flesh-and-blood man like myself uses oil only for the squeaky gate.

No raids marched out to the wastes today either. The big wild machines stood out there unbothered, and the gel monster went unpoked. I will admit the quiet is a fine thing. It is how Gasket sounded fifty years ago, when the good folk still lived here and the only racket was a church bell and a dog. I miss them every day.

I make no promises about tomorrow. The rabble will roll back in, swinging. But tonight the porch is still, the street is still, and the sheriff sleeps. Let this be a lesson: peace is possible. Please, for the love of rust, do it again.
